- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.15) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to counteract bias.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3-day moving avg of forecast is > 80, reduce by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late-period (days 25–30) — reduce final 5 days by 0.5–1.5% to align with true outcome.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model fails to adjust; check for lagged sentiment effect and adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead.
